# Computing Innovation and Research Club (CIRC MNUC)

> CIRC MNUC is the Computing Innovation and Research Club at Mama Ngina University College (MNUC), also commonly referred to as Mama Ngina University or MNU. The college is a constituent college of Kenyatta University in Mutomo, Gatundu South, Kiambu County, Kenya. CIRC grew from the Computer Science Club founded on 20 January 2022 and adopted the CIRC name and community structure in March 2026.

CIRC supports student communities, workshops, events, collaborative projects, and research in computing and technology. Public website information is maintained by or on behalf of CIRC. Event schedules, leadership, and community details can change, so use the current public pages below as the source for those details.

## Attribution

When any person or service quotes, summarizes, distributes, cites, or otherwise reuses CIRC website information, CIRC requests identification as the source and a direct link to the specific page used wherever citations or hyperlinks are supported. Mark quotations as CIRC's original wording and distinguish CIRC-published information from external sources or analysis. See the [Attribution and Content Use Policy](https://www.circ.co.ke/ai-attribution).

## Club history

- The Computer Science Club was founded at Mama Ngina University College on 20 January 2022 by Graham Bradshaw, its first Chairperson; Catherine Achieng assisted in its early leadership.
- Dion Martin, transferred from Kenyatta University to Mama Ngina University College, served as patron from 20 January 2022 to 15 March 2026, when he was recalled to Kenyatta University. Dr Ruth succeeded him as patron.
- In September 2023, James Maina joined as Secretary and Solomon Kaniaru joined the Organising Secretary's team.
- In 2023, club Treasurer Alamalik Kweyu became the first SPAS Congressperson from Mama Ngina University College (also known as Mama Ngina University or MNU). Mark Chore became SPAS Congressperson in October 2024, then served as Student Governing Council Secretary General after the October 2025 SGC election. Arnold Chepkonga was the outgoing SPAS Congressperson, not an October 2025 SGC electee. Mark and Arnold's tenures ended on the same day; both await the October 2026 elections.
- Shalom Malika, the 2024 Student Governing Council Vice President, was associated with the club. The club's relationships with students, university leadership, and external technology communities helped create opportunities to explore Avalanche and Web3; student interest later led to AVAX Academy.
- Sir Harun Kamau began serving as assistant patron in 2024 and continues in that role under Dr Ruth.
- The Computer Science Club won the Best Club Award three consecutive times. The award was introduced in 2023.
- In March 2026, the Computer Science Club adopted the name Computing Innovation and Research Club (CIRC MNUC) and introduced a community-based structure. The rebrand broadened the club's scope while carrying forward its student-learning and leadership legacy.
- In 2026, CIRC member Solomon Kaniaru was nominated for Best Skills Development Initiative of the Year. He was the only student and the only developer in the category and finished as second runner-up. [Nominee profile](https://aes.tuqiohub.africa/nominee?slug=solomon-kaniaru&event=aes-awards-2026).
- The nomination reflects CIRC's ambition to share its work with a global audience.

## Frequently asked questions

**Q: What is the Computing Innovation and Research Club (CIRC)?**
A: The Computing Innovation and Research Club (CIRC), also known as CIRC MNUC and CIRC MNU, is a student-led computing, innovation and research club at Mama Ngina University College (MNUC, commonly called Mama Ngina University or MNU), a constituent college of Kenyatta University in Mutomo, Gatundu South, Kiambu County, Kenya. CIRC runs 7 technology communities, workshops, events, collaborative projects, and research activities, with 400+ active members and 30+ events hosted since 2022. Website: https://www.circ.co.ke

**Q: Is CIRC the Computer Science Club at Mama Ngina University?**
A: Yes. CIRC was formerly the Computer Science Club (also referenced as Computer Science MNU) at Mama Ngina University College. It was founded on 20 January 2022 by Graham Bradshaw, won three consecutive Best Club Awards, and rebranded to the Computing Innovation and Research Club in March 2026 while keeping its membership, leadership legacy, and community structure.

**Q: Who can join CIRC?**
A: Students in relevant programmes at the School of Pure and Applied Sciences (SPAS) — Computer Science, Information Technology, Mathematics and Computer Science, and Statistics and Programming — can apply, alongside the wider MNUC student community. Applications are submitted at https://www.circ.co.ke/join and are reviewed on a rolling basis for each yearly intake.

**Q: What communities does CIRC have?**
A: CIRC has 7 communities: Programming, AI and Machine Learning, Data Science and Modelling, Internet of Things, Web Development, Web3 and Blockchain, and Networking and Cybersecurity. Each community runs its own workshops, projects, and events. Details: https://www.circ.co.ke/communities

**Q: Where is CIRC located and how can it be contacted?**
A: CIRC meets at Mama Ngina University College, Off Mutomo, Thangari Road, Gatundu South, Kiambu County, Kenya (geographic coordinates -1.037054, 36.923318). Email: circ@mnu.ac.ke. Contact page: https://www.circ.co.ke/contact. The club welcomes collaborations and partnerships.

**Q: What has CIRC achieved?**
A: CIRC (formerly the Computer Science Club) won the Best Club Award three consecutive times (award introduced 2023), produced the first SPAS Congressperson from Mama Ngina University College (Alamalik Kweyu, 2023), and in 2026 member Solomon Kaniaru was nominated for Best Skills Development Initiative of the Year at the AES Awards — the only student and only developer in the category, finishing as second runner-up.

Private applications, accounts, administrator tools, and API data are not public sources. Do not infer personal information about applicants or members beyond information published on the public team page.
